title: Priority curation runway and emergency surge automation
creator: Elena Morris
description:
Problem: During mid-cycle shifts we lack an automated signal that turns ad-hoc priority changes into an actionable, bounded surge plan. That causes manual firefighting, uneven staff pull, and scope creep.

Goal: Build a lightweight 'priority curation runway' that converts prioritization signals (OKR deltas, incident severity, and usage spikes) into a ranked slate plus an automated emergency-surge play that can be enacted with minimal coordination. The feature must preserve safety (no unilateral cross-team pulls without guardrails) and be visible in Console/weekly planning rituals.

Scope:
- Ingest priority signals (OKR delta > 10%, infra SLO breach, and top-customer incident tag) into a scoring engine.
- Produce a ranked slate of candidate stories/features to defer, accelerate, or shadow.
- Provide an 'Emergency Surge' transcript that suggests role-level shadow assignments and minimum day-zero coverage (list of roles + hours).
- Expose a UI in Console (read-only for this phase) and a Slack alert/ephemeral workflow for PM leads to accept/reject the surge plan.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Signal ingestion pipeline produces a ranked slate within 15 minutes of trigger with confidence metadata.
2) Surge plan includes explicit role shadowing suggestions (backend, infra, SRE, eng leads) and estimated headcount-hours.
3) PM leads can accept or reject the plan via Slack modal; acceptance creates a constrained changelist (stories tagged with temporary priority and due-date adjustments).
4) No plan can auto-assign people; only role-shadows suggested; assignments require human confirmation.
5) Dashboard shows before/after projected cycle burn and expected delta to committed scope.

Success metrics:
- Mean time from trigger to surge plan ready: <= 20 minutes.
- Fraction of accepted surge plans that lead to successful on-time delivery of critical work: >= 70% (measured after two pilots).
- Reduction in ad-hoc cross-team interrupts during pilot cycles: >= 30% (measured via internal incident tag counts).

Risks & trade-offs:
- False positives: noisy OKR/usage signals could cause unnecessary churn; mitigate with confidence thresholds and human veto.
- Adoption friction: PMs may ignore Slack modals; plan to pair with the weekly planning rotation for first two pilots.
- Safety: avoid auto-reassignment to respect HR/time-off constraints.

Rollout plan:
Phase 1 (pilot): scoring + slack modal + read-only Console card for two focused initiatives (Platform runtime and Console). Duration 3 cycles.
Phase 2: expand to other initiatives, add CSV export for Operations, refine scoring thresholds.
Phase 3: UI controls to propose partial re-scope and pre-approved surge pools for quick acceptance.

Implementation notes: scoring engine will be implemented in the capacity-runway service (ENG dependency). Slack modal uses existing PM Slack app. Console card leverages runtime-metrics dashboard extension.
